page.layout: One page of text, all in one column. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Verse stanzas and headings run down the page, with rules separating the sections.

main_text.p: Dúmque argento alij incubant & auro, Tu Veris fruitur bonis beatus. Sic longum Vigeántque floreántque Candidissima lilia ista florum, Candidissime mi Melisse, tecum. Et nouos quoque gignito Melissos, Noua & lilia lilia ista gignant. Sic longum Vigeántque floreántque Canis lilia cana cum Melissis.
main_text.head: E Graeco.
main_text.p: Diuitiis[?] fruitor, tanquam moriturus, & idem Tanquam Viturus parcito diuitiis. Felix qui Vita & mortis sic diuidis annos, Vita tibi Vt condat, Mors tibi promat opes.
main_text.head: In Superbos, argumento ex moro domestica sumpto, qui intra quiquennium mirabiliter excreuit.
main_text.p: Tenelle nuper furcule, domini manu In arboris spem consite, Iam nunc Virentes arbor attollens comas, Nostrumque inumbrans hortulum.
Quàm nostra forte Vita fertur dispari! Nam tu Vires, ego marceo: Tu Solis æstus & rigorem frigorum Nudo cacumine despicis.

page.notes: The drop-cap initials D and T are large woodcut letters, joined to the following words. The word after the drop cap D ("Diuitiis") is uncertain in the scan and is marked [?]. Horizontal rules separate the sections and are not transcribed. No marginal notes or catchword are printed.
